name: Heirloom Brandywine Tomatoes
description: Prized for their unmatched sweet and tangy vintage tomato flavor, these large pinkish-red heritage tomatoes are harvested fully ripe on the vine.
storageTips: Store stem-down at room temperature away from direct sunlight. Never refrigerate before cutting as cold temps compromise floral aromatics.

name: Honeycrisp & Gala Heritage Apples
description: Orchard-fresh heirloom apples crisp enough to snap, bursting with floral honey sweetness and crisp, juicy refreshment.
nutritionalHighlights: Dietary Pectin Fiber for gut wellness
storageTips: Keep in the crisper drawer with a slightly damp paper towel, or in a cool pantry. Best stored between 32°F and 38°F.

name: Rainbow Swiss Chard & Lacinato Kale
description: Vibrant emerald and ruby stalked greens grown in nutrient-dense volcanic soil. Earthy, slightly sweet, and tender when braised or raw in massaged salads.
nutritionalHighlights: Exceptional Vitamin K for bone health
storageTips: Trim stems, rinse with cool water, spin dry, and wrap gently in a clean kitchen towel inside an airtight vegetable bag.

name: Wild Foraged Chanterelles & Oyster Mushrooms
description: Golden apricot-scented chanterelles and delicate velvet tree oysters hand-harvested by licensed foragers from Pacific Northwest coastal ridges.
storageTips: Store in a breathable brown paper bag in your refrigerator main shelf. Never store in sealed plastic, and brush dry before sauteing.

name: Sweet Italian Genovese Basil & Fresh Mint
description: Aromatic living bunches cut fresh morning of market day, packed with volatile essential oils and sweet peppery warmth for pesto and teas.
nutritionalHighlights: Rich in Vitamin A precursor carotenoids
storageTips: Place cut stems in a small glass jar of fresh water on your kitchen counter like fresh flowers. Do not chill basil in the fridge.

name: Sweet Baby French Carrots & Golden Beets
description: Tender young roots pulled from sandy loam soils with feathery green tops intact. Naturally sweet, candy-crisp, and delicious roasted whole.
nutritionalHighlights: Soluble fiber and nitrates for circulation
Rich in minerals like zinc and biotin
storageTips: Cut off green leafy tops 1 inch above crown immediately to prevent moisture loss from the root. Keep in a sealed crisper container for 3+ weeks.

name: Artisanal Herb Chevre & Raw Milk Cheddar
description: Small-batch farmstead cheeses produced by grass-fed dairy cooperatives, flavored with garden rosemary, cracked peppercorn, and lavender.
storageTips: Wrap in parchment or breathable cheese paper before placing in a loose box in the warmest part of your refrigerator.

name: Wildflower Raw Mountain Honeycomb
description: Unpasteurized, unfiltered honey extracted straight from solar-warmed hives in alpine meadows, rich in local wildflower pollens and enzymes.
storageTips: Store in sealed glass jar at room temperature indefinitely. If crystallization occurs, place jar in a warm water bath.

name: Country Sourdough Boule & Spelt Bread
description: Naturally leavened over 36 hours using organic regionally milled stoneground grains and spring water with a blistered crunchy crust.
nutritionalHighlights: Pre-digested gluten via wild lactobacillus fermentation
Zero synthetic preservatives or dough conditioners
storageTips: Store cut-side down on a wooden breadboard or inside a linen bread sack for 3 days. Freeze sliced for long-term enjoyment.

name: Pasture-Raised Heritage Brown Eggs
description: Laid by heritage breed hens roaming freely on certified green clover pastures. Noticeable deep golden-orange yolks and sturdy shells.
nutritionalHighlights: Triple Omega-3 fatty acids vs conventional
storageTips: Keep in their carton on an interior refrigerator shelf (not in the door) to maintain steady 35°-40°F temperature.

name: Butternut Squash & Sugar Pie Pumpkins
description: Hard-rind winter squash cured under late summer sun. Silky roasted texture with nutty, sweet brown-butter undertones.
storageTips: Cured squash can be kept in a dry, ventilated, cool spot (50-55°F) for up to 3 to 6 months.

name: Organic Marionberries & Autumn Raspberries
description: Fragile jewel berries picked the morning of sale. Explosive sweet-tart berry fragrance ideal for pies, preserves, and yogurt parfaits.
storageTips: Do not wash until immediately before eating. Store in single layer on a paper towel in a ventilated container.

name: French Breakfast Radishes & Purple Kohlrabi
description: Crisp oblong radishes with white tips and peppery crunch, paired with crisp sweet kohlrabi bulbs perfect for slaws.
storageTips: Remove greens and store radishes in a container filled with cool water in the fridge to keep extra crisp.

name: Small-Batch Blackberry Fig Jam & Preserves
description: Simmered in copper kettles using whole fruit and organic raw cane sugar. No artificial pectin or coloring.
storageTips: Once opened, store refrigerated and consume within 60 days.

name: Organic Rosemary, Sage & Garden Thyme
description: Woody perennial culinary herbs bursting with fragrant pinene and thymol essential oils for hearty soups, roasts, and marinades.
storageTips: Wrap loosely in dry paper towels and keep in an unsealed bag in the crisper drawer, or hang upside down to dry.

name: Crisp Asian Pears & Autumn Plums
description: Orchard-ripened round golden Asian pears with a delicate water-melon crispness and floral notes, complemented by tart Italian prune plums.
storageTips: Keep on counter until aromatic, then refrigerate for up to 3 weeks.
